articles.title: Validation of a standardized question and a numerical rating scale for assessment of patient satisfaction after knee arthroplasty at one and two years.
articles.authors: Clement ND, Karimaghaei D, Afzal I, Haddad FS, Kader DF
articles.population: Patients undergoing knee arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 7,644 knee arthroplasties in 6,690 patients (5,893 with one-year follow-up, 4,879 with two-year follow-up)
articles.outcomes: Patient satisfaction measured on a 0-100 numerical rating scale at one and two years after surgery, correlated with Oxford Knee Scores and EQ-5D-3L scores
articles.take_home: A simple satisfaction question scored 0 to 100 is a reliable way to measure how happy patients are after knee replacement surgery. Most patients rated their satisfaction as 90 or higher, and satisfaction levels stayed much the same between one and two years after surgery.

articles.title: Rivaroxaban Then Aspirin vs. Aspirin Alone after Total Hip or Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Shivakumar S, Matino D, Zukor D, Kahn SR, Vincent G, Mundi R, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing total hip or total knee arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 5429 patients randomised
articles.outcomes: Symptomatic venous thromboembolism (deep-vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism) at 90 days; major bleeding or clinically relevant non-major bleeding
articles.take_home: Aspirin alone was as effective as rivaroxaban followed by aspirin at preventing blood clots after hip or knee replacement surgery, with similar rates of bleeding. This suggests aspirin alone may be a suitable option for preventing clots after these operations.

articles.title: Preoperative Sepsis Is Associated with an Elevated Rate of Periprosthetic Joint Infection and Mortality Following Total Hip Arthroplasty in a Time-Dependent Manner.
articles.authors: Alhankawi AR, Holle AM, Renfree SP, Braithwaite CL, Verhey JT, Deckey DG, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using national insurance database
articles.population: Patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty who had sepsis within two years beforehand, compared to matched controls without sepsis
articles.sample_size: Not stated in abstract
articles.outcomes: Periprosthetic joint infection, postoperative sepsis, acute kidney injury, urinary tract infection, pneumonia, readmission, wound dehiscence, dislocation, mortality, deep vein thrombosis, and periprosthetic fracture at 90 days and two years
articles.take_home: Patients who had sepsis in the two years before hip replacement had higher rates of infection, other complications and death than those without sepsis. The risk was highest when sepsis occurred within six to twelve months of the operation.

articles.title: Sport-discipline and age-related differences in knee extensor musculotendinous morphology and function.
articles.authors: Cesanelli L, Pernigoni M, Streckis V, Kamandulis S, Satkunskiene D, Rodriguez-Longobardo C, et al.
articles.population: Male competitive athletes: cyclists, basketball players, and ice hockey players
articles.sample_size: 90 athletes (15 youth and 15 elite per sport discipline)
articles.outcomes: Knee extensor muscle thickness, patellar tendon size, muscle strength, jumping ability, anterior knee pain, and knee injury history
articles.take_home: Different sports place different demands on the knee, with cyclists having larger muscles relative to body weight but less tendon stress, whilst basketball and ice hockey players showed better jumping ability. Elite athletes reported more knee pain and injuries than younger athletes, despite their muscles and tendons developing proportionally as they progress.

articles.title: Joint-specific mechanical work during overground running in athletes with anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction history.
articles.authors: Abdolmaleki S, Esmaeili H, Salari-Esker F, Rahimi Khoygani M, Ziaei M, Bashiri B
articles.population: Male recreational athletes with and without anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction history
articles.sample_size: 44 participants (22 with ACLR, 22 healthy controls)
articles.outcomes: Mechanical work distribution (negative and positive work) at the hip, knee and ankle joints during running stance phase
articles.take_home: Athletes who have had anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction shift their running mechanics to reduce load on the reconstructed knee by absorbing more energy at the hip and generating more power at the ankle. This compensation pattern suggests rehabilitation should focus on strengthening the whole leg rather than just the knee.

articles.title: Super-acute massive osteolysis of the femoral head after acetabular fracture fixation : a comparative study with conventional post-traumatic osteonecrosis requiring total hip arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Yu YH, Lai CY, Chen IJ, Hsu YH, Chou YC
articles.population: Adult patients who underwent acetabular fracture surgery and subsequently needed hip replacement
articles.sample_size: 31 patients (12 with super-acute massive osteolysis, 19 with conventional osteonecrosis)
articles.outcomes: Clinical and radiological features of super-acute massive femoral head osteolysis compared with conventional post-traumatic osteonecrosis; factors associated with super-acute osteolysis
articles.take_home: Super-acute massive osteolysis of the femoral head is a rare but serious complication after acetabular fracture surgery that occurs despite good surgical fixation, and is more likely in older patients. The condition appears to result from biological factors rather than surgical technique, so close follow-up imaging and early preparation for hip replacement is recommended for older patients at risk.

articles.title: Miscorrection in coronal plane osteotomies around the knee-Current concepts.
articles.authors: Dawson MJ, Mabrouk A, Nejima S, Elson D, van Heerwaarden RJ
articles.population: Patients undergoing osteotomy surgery around the knee
articles.outcomes: Prevention and understanding of miscorrection in coronal plane osteotomies; comparison of computer-assisted navigation and patient-specific instrumentation technologies
articles.take_home: Miscorrection after knee osteotomy surgery involves many interconnected factors in planning, technique and rehabilitation. There is no single correction target that works for all patients, so individualised planning based on factors like joint line angle is important to achieve accurate results.

articles.title: Concomitant meniscal repair and resection are not associated with ACL reoperation, and successful meniscal repair preserves patient-reported outcomes: A 2-year retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Kekki C, Cristiani R, Stalman A, von Essen C
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction with or without concomitant meniscal procedure
articles.sample_size: 5387 primary ACLRs (1305 with meniscal repair, 1097 with meniscal resection, mean age 29.7 years, 51% male)
articles.outcomes: Two-year ACL reoperation rates, subsequent meniscal procedures, patient-reported outcome measures (KOOS score), minimal important change, patient-acceptable symptom state and treatment failure
articles.take_home: Meniscal repair during ACL surgery led to more follow-up meniscal procedures than repair or isolated surgery alone, but successful repairs had similar patient outcomes to ACL surgery alone. Lateral meniscal repairs had better results than medial or combined repairs.

articles.title: No clear benefit of patient-specific instruments over conventional instrumentation in unicompartmental knee arthroplasty: A secondary analysis of a multicentre randomised trial with 5-year follow-up.
articles.authors: Leenders AM, Schotanus MGM, Most J, Van Geenen RCI, Boonen B
articles.study_type: Secondary analysis of a multicentre randomised controlled trial
articles.population: Patients undergoing unicompartmental knee arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 120 patients (56 patient-specific instruments, 59 conventional instrumentation)
articles.outcomes: Revision rate, Oxford Knee Score, Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Arthritis Index, EuroQol-5D, pain scores, and forgotten joint score at 5-year follow-up
articles.take_home: Patient-specific instruments and conventional instrumentation produced similar results for knee replacement, with no clear advantage of one method over the other. Both groups showed good improvement in pain and function after surgery.

articles.title: Cryostick pre-cooling reduces pain during intra-articular knee injections: a randomized, contralateral-controlled trial.
articles.authors: Sutthapakti B, Luanghirun P, Khasemsiri R, Sukha K, Wanitcharoenporn W, Laoruengthana A
articles.population: Adults with bilateral knee osteoarthritis
articles.sample_size: 50 patients (100 knees)
articles.outcomes: Pain during needle insertion and at 5 minutes after injection, bleeding area, and patient satisfaction
articles.take_home: Using a cryostick (a cooling device at minus 20 degrees Celsius) for 20 seconds before knee injection significantly reduced pain during the procedure and at 5 minutes afterwards, whilst also reducing bleeding. Patients were also more satisfied with the injection when the cryostick was used.

articles.title: Functional alignment robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty with tibial varus limited to 6 degrees yields greater early postoperative pain improvement in patients with preoperative MPTA >/=84 degrees compared with MPTA <84 degrees .
articles.authors: Neo BXB, Chua HYJ, Pang HN, Tay KD, Yeo SJ, Liow MHL
articles.population: Patients with varus knee deformity undergoing robotic-assisted functional alignment total knee arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 93 patients (49 with MPTA <84 degrees, 44 with MPTA >/=84-89 degrees)
articles.outcomes: Knee Society Knee and Function Scores, Oxford Knee Score, SF-36 scores, minimal clinically important difference achievement at 6 months
articles.take_home: Patients whose natural tibial alignment could be fully restored (MPTA >/=84 degrees) had better pain relief after robotic knee replacement surgery at 6 months. However, both groups showed good overall improvement and satisfaction, suggesting the surgery works well regardless of how severely bowed the shin bone was before surgery.

articles.title: While no objective measure exists to capture TKA instability, motion analysis instruments and radiographic stress tests show most potential: a scoping review.
articles.authors: Droogsma T, Tuijthof GJM, van Laarhoven SN, Heesterbeek PJC
articles.population: Patients with total knee replacement (TKA), stable and unstable
articles.sample_size: 29 studies reviewed
articles.outcomes: Ability of objective measures (stress radiographs, motion analysis, wearable sensors) and patient-reported measures to distinguish stable from unstable knee replacements
articles.take_home: There is no single agreed test to diagnose an unstable knee replacement, but stress X-rays and motion analysis during weight-bearing activities show the most promise for identifying when a knee replacement has become loose or unstable.

articles.title: A Century of Orthopaedic Excellence with Global Impact: Instituto de Ortopedia y Traumatologia "Carlos E. Ottolenghi" at Hospital Italiano de Buenos Aires.
articles.authors: Buttaro M, Ranalletta M, Slullitel PA, Rossi LA, Aponte LA, Ayerza MA, et al.
articles.population: Orthopaedic residents, fellows, and staff surgeons at Instituto de Ortopedia y Traumatologia, Hospital Italiano de Buenos Aires
articles.sample_size: 180 residents and 160 fellows trained over 25 years
articles.outcomes: Institutional milestones including pioneering procedures (first hip and knee replacements in Americas and Argentina), adoption of advanced surgical techniques, and production of over 500 indexed publications in the last 10 years
articles.take_home: This Argentine orthopaedic institute became a world-leading centre of excellence through pioneering surgical innovations including early hip and knee replacements, and continues to train surgeons who hold leadership positions globally. The institute demonstrates that excellence in orthopaedics can develop anywhere through commitment to innovation and rigorous training.

articles.title: Weaning in INfant hip DYsplasia (WINDY) study: weaning of brace treatment versus immediate cessation for developmental dysplasia of the hip : study protocol for a randomized multicentre feasibility study.
articles.authors: Craven J, Kirk R, Griffin XL, Conroy E, Carpenter EC, Llewellyn-Stanton L, et al.
articles.population: Infants with developmental dysplasia of the hip treated with Pavlik harness who have achieved hip normalization on ultrasound
articles.outcomes: Recruitment rates, proportion randomized, parental engagement and compliance, acceptability of weaning versus immediate cessation, measurement properties of EMBRACE questionnaire, feasibility of using Smart4NIPE data for trial outcomes
articles.take_home: This is a feasibility study to test whether a larger trial comparing gradual weaning of a hip brace to stopping it immediately is possible. The study will check if families will take part, complete questionnaires, and follow the treatment plan.

articles.title: Revision periacetabular osteotomy enhances joint function and activity level after failure of redirectional pelvic osteotomy at skeletal maturity.
articles.authors: Fischer M, Nitsch A, Goronzy J, Kasabji F, Hofer A, Wassilew GI
articles.population: Patients with hip dysplasia who had revision periacetabular osteotomy (R-PAO) after previous failed pelvic osteotomy, compared to patients having primary PAO
articles.sample_size: 13 revision PAO patients matched 1:3 with 39 primary PAO patients
articles.outcomes: Pain, joint function (Modified Harris Hip Score and International Hip outcome tool-12), activity level (UCLA activity scale), and postoperative anterior hip coverage
articles.take_home: Revision hip surgery after failed previous osteotomy can improve pain and function, but patients end up with worse outcomes than those having primary surgery because they start in a more damaged state. Better outcomes after either type of surgery were linked to better joint condition before surgery, lower body weight, and good hip socket coverage after the operation.

articles.title: Association between superficial surgical site infection and revision after primary total hip arthroplasty: a cohort study of 3,242 patients.
articles.authors: Pollmann CT, Thomas OMT, Rotterud JHM, Dale H, Wulf MWH, Skramm I
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 3,242 patients (27 with superficial surgical site infection)
articles.outcomes: Risk of revision hip arthroplasty for any cause within minimum 4-year follow-up
articles.take_home: Superficial surgical site infections after hip replacement were not associated with an increased need for revision surgery. The study found no evidence that superficial infections lead to worse long-term outcomes requiring further operations.

articles.title: High prevalence of muscle stability deficits in semi-professional football players-Adaptive Force assessment reveals selective impairment of holding capacity with preserved maximal strength: A cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Schaefer LV, Bittmann FN, Ulrich J, Prill R, Becker R
articles.population: Male semi-professional football players
articles.sample_size: 23 players
articles.outcomes: Prevalence of muscle stability deficits measured by Adaptive Force; comparison of holding capacity versus maximal strength; discriminative capacity of stability assessment versus conventional hamstrings-to-quadriceps ratio
articles.take_home: Most football players (83%) had muscle stability problems, particularly in hip and hamstring muscles, but these deficits were not detected by standard strength tests. A new assessment measuring holding capacity rather than pushing strength was much better at identifying these problems.

articles.title: Primary anterior cruciate ligament tears are associated with a shift from varus-dominant to neutral and valgus coronal alignment phenotypes.
articles.authors: Mortazavi SMJ, Razzaghof M, Soleimani M, Rezaee H, Naghizadeh H, Mortazavi A, et al.
articles.population: Patients with primary anterior cruciate ligament tears and age- and sex-matched healthy controls
articles.sample_size: 192 ACL-injured patients and 193 healthy controls (384 and 386 knees respectively)
articles.outcomes: Coronal alignment phenotypes measured by hip-knee-ankle angle, femoral mechanical angle, tibial mechanical angle and joint line convergence angle, classified using Hirschmann's functional classification and coronal plane alignment of the knee system
articles.take_home: Knees with ACL tears showed a shift away from varus (bow-legged) alignment towards more neutral and valgus (knock-kneed) alignment compared to healthy knees. The pattern in the uninjured knee of ACL patients suggests some people may have a constitutional predisposition to these alignment patterns, though the greater shift in injured knees indicates the injury itself or changes after injury also play a role.

articles.title: Early arthrogenic muscle inhibition is the dominant predictor of persistent quadriceps inhibition after total knee arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Barrera Uso M, Fayard JM, Vieira TD, Bondoux L, Selmi TAS, Bonnin M, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee replacement
articles.sample_size: 229 consecutive patients
articles.outcomes: Arthrogenic muscle inhibition (quadriceps weakness) assessed at pre-operation, 30 days and 60 days after surgery using clinical classification
articles.take_home: Muscle inhibition around the knee is common after knee replacement, affecting nearly half of patients at one month but improving to one in five by two months. Early muscle inhibition is the strongest predictor of ongoing problems, along with older age, pre-existing weakness, severe post-operative pain and obesity.

articles.title: The Reconstructive Pelvic Anatomy classification system : a valid and reliable classification system for pelvic reconstruction.
articles.authors: Collins WJJ, Franks D, Harris IA, Sidhu VS, Guzman M, Stalley PD, et al.
articles.population: Orthopaedic surgeons performing pelvic reconstruction
articles.sample_size: 23 surgeons for content validity assessment, 18 surgeons for both surveys, 20 pelvic reconstructions evaluated
articles.outcomes: Content validity (Item-Content Validity Index), construct validity (agreement between observers and authors), interobserver agreement, intraobserver agreement (measured using kappa statistic)
articles.take_home: The Reconstructive Pelvic Anatomy classification system is a valid and reliable tool for describing pelvic reconstructions and helping surgeons communicate about complex cases. Most domains showed good agreement between different surgeons and consistent results when the same surgeon assessed cases again.

articles.title: Acute Kidney Injury Following Antibiotic-Loaded Spacer Insertion in Two-Stage Knee Arthroplasty Revision for Periprosthetic Joint Infection: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Youmbi CT, Santos A, Bridger A, Backstein D, Ekhtiari S, Wolfstadt JI
articles.population: Patients undergoing two-stage revision knee replacement for infection
articles.sample_size: 152 patients
articles.outcomes: Acute kidney injury (AKI) rates after spacer insertion; 6.6% after first stage and 2.6% after second stage. 86% of AKI cases resolved within one month.
articles.take_home: Very high-dose antibiotic-loaded spacers used in two-stage knee replacement revision caused temporary kidney problems in a small number of patients, but these problems usually resolved within a month and were not related to pre-existing kidney disease.

articles.title: Tourniquet Use in Cemented Total Knee Arthroplasty: Small Gains in Fixation, No Clear Benefit in Aseptic Loosening. A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.authors: Klincke V, Descamps T, Tampere T, Arnout N, Victor J, Vermue H
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary cemented total knee arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 54,561 knees across 26 studies (13,540 without tourniquet, 40,931 with full tourniquet, 90 with partial tourniquet)
articles.outcomes: Cement penetration, radiostereometric analysis, radiolucent lines, aseptic loosening, and revision surgery rates
articles.take_home: Using a tourniquet during knee replacement surgery led to slightly better cement penetration and fewer overall revisions, but this did not reliably improve long-term fixation or reduce aseptic loosening specifically.

articles.title: Concomitant cartilage restoration does not demonstrate consistent additional clinical benefit in medial patellofemoral ligament reconstruction: A systematic review.
articles.authors: Duru DO, Wade D, Bouchard MD, Vivekanantha P, Malik SS, Skelley NW, et al.
articles.population: Adults undergoing medial patellofemoral ligament reconstruction with cartilage lesions
articles.sample_size: 18 studies, 1632 patients, mean age 22.2 years
articles.outcomes: Pain and function measured by KOOS Pain, Kujala and IKDC scores; complication rates
articles.take_home: Medial patellofemoral ligament reconstruction improved pain and function in patients with cartilage damage, but adding cartilage repair procedures did not provide additional benefit compared to reconstruction alone. Cartilage repair procedures were associated with more complications.

articles.title: Changes in sex distribution in Achilles tendon rupture literature over 74 years: A systematic review.
articles.authors: Potter MN, Mlecko J, Christensen M, Aufwerber S, Katz SE, Pohlig RT, et al.
articles.study_type: Systematic review of 74 years of Achilles tendon rupture literature
articles.population: People with primary complete Achilles tendon rupture
articles.sample_size: 532 articles analysed, covering studies from 1948 to 2022
articles.outcomes: Sex distribution changes over time; percentage of females in study populations; proportion of articles reporting sex-disaggregated data
articles.take_home: Studies of Achilles tendon rupture show a gradual increase in the proportion of women participants over 74 years, rising from around 7% in 1990 to 39% in 2015, but men still make up about 81% of cases overall. Most research articles do not report separate results for men and women, which limits our understanding of how this injury affects each sex differently.

articles.title: Anterior open wedge high tibial osteotomy for slope correction as a successful method in PCL insufficiency-Radiological and clinical results of a cohort study.
articles.authors: Dickschas J, Sendner T, Schubert I, Simon M, Neumaier M
articles.population: Patients with chronic posterior cruciate ligament insufficiency and reduced posterior tibial slope
articles.sample_size: 11 patients (9 male, 2 female)
articles.outcomes: Lysholm Knee Score improved from 59.0 to 83.0 points; Tegner Activity Scale increased from 3.0 to 5.3; posterior tibial slope angle corrected by mean 9.2 degrees; 8 of 11 patients reported satisfactory knee stability without giving way
articles.take_home: Anterior open wedge high tibial osteotomy significantly improved knee function and stability in patients with chronic PCL insufficiency, with most patients achieving satisfactory results without needing further surgery. However, functional outcomes remained below pre-injury levels.

articles.title: The association between body mass index, age and severity of musculoskeletal injuries sustained during high school contact sports: A 15-year epidemiological study.
articles.authors: Bajaj P, Workman C, Angileri H, Watson S, Cho S, Tanenbaum J, et al.
articles.population: High school contact sports athletes (boys' and girls' soccer, basketball, wrestling and football)
articles.sample_size: 33,486 musculoskeletal injuries reported (representing approximately 11 million injuries nationally weighted)
articles.outcomes: Injury severity measured by time to return to pre-injury activity
articles.take_home: Body mass index and age showed statistically significant but clinically negligible associations with injury recovery time in some sports, meaning they are not useful in predicting how long an athlete will take to recover from a musculoskeletal injury.

articles.title: Intraoperative Surgical Smoke During Arthroplasty: Early Unhealthy-Level Exposure and Approach-Dependent Risk.
articles.authors: Tsuchiya R, Suzuki R, Yano S, Ikenoue S, Mimura M, Sameda H, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary arthroplasty surgery
articles.sample_size: 83 patients (20 bipolar hemiarthroplasties, 35 total hip arthroplasties, 28 total knee arthroplasties)
articles.outcomes: Intraoperative fine particle (PM2.5) concentrations measured and mapped to Air Quality Index categories; percentage of cases reaching unhealthy air quality levels
articles.take_home: Hip and knee replacement surgery via certain approaches produced harmful levels of surgical smoke in most cases, whilst anterior hip replacements had much lower smoke exposure. Operating room teams should use smoke evacuation systems and high-efficiency masks to reduce exposure to potentially harmful surgical smoke.

articles.title: Osteochondral Autograft Transfer for Focal Osteochondral Defects of the Knee: Indications, Technique, Outcomes, and Future Directions.
articles.authors: Strony JT, Ina JG, Apostolakos JM, Calcei JG, Karns MR, Ode GE, et al.
articles.population: Young, active patients with focal full-thickness articular cartilage defects of the knee
articles.outcomes: Return-to-sport rates (often >85% within 6 months), functional improvements, cartilage and bone restoration
articles.take_home: Osteochondral autograft transfer is a durable, single-stage procedure that restores cartilage and bone in young patients with small to medium knee cartilage defects (1 to 4 cm²), with most patients returning to sport within 6 months. Results are less reliable for defects larger than 3 cm² or in older patients with lower activity demands.

articles.title: Protocol for Novel Perioperative Optimization of Obese Osteoarthritic Patients pending Total Knee Replacement with glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (NPO-OOPS-TKR) : a pilot randomized controlled trial.
articles.authors: Lau LCM, Lui TWD, Wen C, Zhu L, Lin S, Leung TKC, et al.
articles.population: Adults aged 40 to 80 years with obesity (BMI ≥27 kg/m²) listed for primary total knee replacement
articles.sample_size: 54 participants
articles.outcomes: Primary outcomes: feasibility measures (recruitment, adherence, tolerability, retention). Exploratory outcomes: pain, body weight, patient-reported outcomes, perioperative complications
articles.take_home: This is a pilot study to test whether using semaglutide (a weight loss medication) before and after knee replacement surgery is feasible and acceptable in older Asian adults with obesity. The study will gather information to decide if a larger trial is possible.

articles.title: Similar patient-reported outcomes 6 months after unicompartmental and total knee replacement for osteoarthritis: a prospective cohort study of 60,145 patients from the Australian Orthopaedic Association National Joint Replacement Registry.
articles.authors: Fidler HL, Kiroff GK, Du P, Ackerman IN, Oakey H, Lewis PL
articles.population: Patients with knee osteoarthritis undergoing unicompartmental or total knee replacement
articles.sample_size: 60,145 patients (3,329 UKA, 56,816 TKA)
articles.outcomes: Patient-reported outcomes at 6 months: Oxford Knee Scores, EQ-5D-5L quality of life, knee pain rating, satisfaction, and patient-perceived change
articles.take_home: Unicompartmental and total knee replacements produced similarly good results 6 months after surgery, with no meaningful difference between the two procedures in terms of pain relief, function, or quality of life improvements, although patients having unicompartmental replacement were slightly more likely to report satisfaction.
